records.source: וּֽלְנָעֳמִ֞י מוֹדַ֣ע לְאִישָׁ֗הּ אִ֚ישׁ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל מִמִּשְׁפַּ֖חַת אֱלִימֶ֑לֶךְ וּשְׁמ֖וֹ בֹּֽעַז׃
records.gloss: And to Naomi [was] a relative of her husband, a man mighty of wealth, from [the] clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.
pieces: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a man of wealth and standing from the clan of Elimelech. His name was Boaz.

L.1: Now Naomi had a relative of her husband, a man mighty in wealth, from the clan of Elimelech, and his name [was] Boaz.

R.1: Naomi had a relative on her husband's side named Boaz. He was a rich and respected man from Elimelech's clan.

decisions.choice: a man mighty in wealth: a man of substance and good name
decisions.reason: The phrase can describe a strong warrior (Judges 6:12; 11:1), but here, in a story of fields and harvest, it means a man of wealth, ability and standing in his town. The same word chayil is used of Ruth in 3:11, "a woman of worth", so the two are matched before they meet.

decisions.choice: relative: one known to the family, a kinsman
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the reading tradition give two slightly different forms of this word here, but both name a man close to the family: a relative or one known as kin. A word from the same root names Boaz as "our relative" in 3:2. Verse 20 shows how close he is.

decisions.choice: the narrator tells the reader first
decisions.reason: The verse interrupts the story to introduce Boaz before Ruth meets him. The reader knows who owns the field in verse 3; Ruth and Naomi do not learn it until verse 19.

decisions.choice: a man of wealth and standing (Balanced); a rich and respected man (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give both sides of the phrase, his wealth and his good name. Literal keeps "mighty in wealth".

records.heading: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz

records.source: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ ר֨וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶֽל־נָעֳמִ֗י אֵֽלְכָה־נָּ֤א הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וַאֲלַקֳטָּ֣הבַשִׁבֳּלִ֔יםאַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶמְצָא־חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ לְכִ֥י בִתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Ruth the Moabite to Naomi, let me go, please, [to] the field and let me glean among the ears behind [one] who I find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, go, my daughter.
pieces: Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and glean ears of grain behind anyone who will look on me with favor." Naomi answered her, "Go, my daughter."

L.2: And Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Please let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain behind [someone] in whose eyes I find favor." And she said to her, "Go, my daughter."

R.2: Ruth, the woman from Moab, said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields. I will pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."

decisions.choice: glean: gather the grain the harvesters left behind
decisions.reason: God's law told landowners not to reap to the very edges of a field or go back for what was dropped or forgotten, but to leave it for the poor, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow (Leviticus 19:9-10; 23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19). Ruth is poor, foreign and widowed, so she has a right to glean.

decisions.choice: find favor in his eyes: be treated kindly
decisions.reason: To find favor in someone's eyes is to win his goodwill. Even with the law on her side, Ruth hopes to find a landowner or reaper who will let her glean and treat her well; the same phrase comes back in verses 10 and 13.

decisions.choice: Ruth the Moabite: her foreign origin kept in view
decisions.reason: The narrator keeps calling her "the Moabite" (1:22; 2:21) and others do too (verse 6). The story never lets the reader forget that a foreign woman is the one who shows such loyalty.

decisions.choice: pick up the grain the harvesters leave behind, if someone will be kind enough to let me
decisions.reason: Readable explains what gleaning is and says what "finding favor" means here: someone letting her glean.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ וַתָּבוֹא֙ וַתְּלַקֵּ֣ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקֹּצְרִ֑ים וַיִּ֣קֶר מִקְרֶ֔הָ חֶלְקַ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ לְבֹ֔עַז אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת אֱלִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters; and chanced her chance [on the] portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from [the] clan of Elimelech.
pieces: So she set out, came to a field and gleaned behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to the part of the field that belonged to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.

L.3: So she went and came and gleaned in the field behind the harvesters, and her chance chanced upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who [was] from the clan of Elimelech.

R.3: So Ruth went out and began picking up grain behind the harvesters. It just so happened that she was working in a field that belonged to Boaz, the man from Elimelech's clan.

decisions.choice: her chance chanced: it happened, as far as she knew, by chance
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun come from the same root, a doubled way of saying it just happened. From Ruth's point of view it was luck. The narrator, who has already introduced Boaz (verse 1), lets the reader see more: Naomi will praise the LORD for it in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the portion of the field: one family's plot
decisions.reason: The farmland around a town was one open stretch divided into family plots without fences. A gleaner could move from one owner's strip to another without knowing whose land she was on.

decisions.choice: as it happened (Balanced); it just so happened (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense of chance in plain words; Literal keeps the doubled Hebrew "her chance chanced".

records.source: וְהִנֵּה־בֹ֗עַז בָּ֚א מִבֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים יְהוָ֣ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And look, Boaz [was] coming from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, Yahweh [be] with you. And they said to him, may bless you Yahweh.
pieces: Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem. He greeted the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" and they answered him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"

L.4: And look, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [be] with you!" And they said to him, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"

R.4: Just then Boaz came out from Bethlehem. He said to the harvesters, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you!" They answered, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you!"

decisions.choice: and look: Boaz arrives at that very moment
decisions.reason: The word hinneh draws attention to what happens next, as if the reader were watching. Ruth has only just come to the field when its owner appears.

decisions.choice: greeting and reply as blessings
decisions.reason: People greeted one another with a blessing in the LORD's name (Judges 6:12; Psalm 129:8). The exchange shows a landowner and workers on good terms, and a man who speaks of God in everyday life.

decisions.choice: just then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express hinneh by its timing; Literal keeps "look".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בֹּ֨עַז֙ לְנַעֲר֔וֹ הַנִּצָּ֖ב עַל־הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֑ים לְמִ֖י הַנַּעֲרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And said Boaz to his young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, to whom [is] this young woman?
pieces: Boaz asked his servant who was in charge of the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"

L.5: And Boaz said to his young man who was set over the harvesters, "To whom [does] this young woman [belong]?"

R.5: Boaz asked the man in charge of his harvesters, "Who is that young woman? What family is she from?"

decisions.choice: his young man set over the harvesters: his foreman
decisions.reason: Na'ar means a young man, and often a young man in someone's service, a worker or attendant. This one has been put in charge of the reapers.

decisions.choice: to whom does she belong?: what household is she part of
decisions.reason: A woman was known by the household she belonged to: her father's, her husband's, or a master's. Boaz asks not her name but her family and place, and the answer in verse 6 tells him exactly that.

decisions.choice: young woman: na'arah
decisions.reason: The word is used of a girl or young woman, often unmarried and sometimes in service. Ruth is a widow but still young; Boaz is older (3:10).

decisions.choice: servant (Balanced); the man in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "young man", the word's basic sense; Balanced and Readable say what he was to Boaz.

decisions.choice: What family is she from?
decisions.reason: Readable adds the second question to show what "whose" means here.

records.source: וַיַּ֗עַן הַנַּ֛עַר הַנִּצָּ֥ב עַל־הַקּוֹצְרִ֖ים וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נַעֲרָ֤ה מֽוֹאֲבִיָּה֙ הִ֔יא הַשָּׁ֥בָה עִֽם־נָעֳמִ֖י מִשְּׂדֵ֥ה מוֹאָֽב׃
records.gloss: And answered the young man, the [one] stationed over the harvesters, and said, a young woman, a Moabite, [is] she, the [one who] returned with Naomi from [the] field of Moab.
pieces: The servant in charge of the harvesters answered, "She is a young Moabite woman, the one who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.

L.6: And the young man who was set over the harvesters answered and said, "She [is] a young Moabite woman, the [one] who returned with Naomi from the country of Moab.

R.6: The man answered, "She is the young woman from Moab who came back with Naomi.

decisions.choice: returned: came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Ruth had never lived in Bethlehem, yet the same verb is used of her as of Naomi (1:22). By joining Naomi's people (1:16) she has, in a sense, come home with her.

decisions.choice: a young Moabite woman: her origin first
decisions.reason: The foreman's first words are that she is a Moabite. Moab and Israel had a hard history (Numbers 22-25; Deuteronomy 23:4-5), so this is the first thing people notice about her.

decisions.choice: the field of Moab: the country of Moab
decisions.reason: The word for field also means open country or territory, as in 1:1 and 1:6.

decisions.choice: from Moab ... came back with Naomi
decisions.reason: Readable says "from Moab" once, so the country is not named twice in one short sentence.

records.source: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲלַקֳטָה־נָּא֙ וְאָסַפְתִּ֣י בָֽעֳמָרִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י הַקּוֹצְרִ֑ים וַתָּב֣וֹא וַֽתַּעֲמ֗וֹד מֵאָ֤ז הַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וְעַד־עַ֔תָּה זֶ֛ה שִׁבְתָּ֥הּ הַבַּ֖יִת מְעָֽט׃
records.gloss: And she said, let me glean, please, and I will gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters. And she came and has stood from then, the morning, and until now; this her sitting [in] the house [is a] little.
pieces: She said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came, and she has been on her feet from early morning until now, except for a short rest in the shelter."

L.7: And she said, 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' So she came and has stood from the morning until now; her sitting in the house [has been] little."

R.7: She asked me, 'Please let me pick up grain among the bundles behind the harvesters.' She came early this morning, and she has been working ever since. She has only stopped for a little while to rest in the shelter."

decisions.choice: her sitting in the house has been little: she has hardly rested
alternatives: she has stood waiting since morning
she has not rested even a little
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is very hard in the Hebrew, word for word "this her sitting the house little". The likeliest sense is that she has kept working since morning and rested only briefly in the field shelter. Others take it to mean that she has stood waiting for permission since morning, or read it as "she has not rested in the field even a little", as the ancient Greek translation does. The wording may have been damaged in copying.

decisions.choice: gather among the sheaves: glean where the cut grain lies bundled
decisions.reason: Gleaners usually followed behind once the sheaves had been tied and taken away. Ruth asks to gather among the sheaves themselves, more than the law granted, and in verse 15 Boaz allows it. The words may also mean that she asked to gather her gleanings into bundles.

decisions.choice: the house: the field shelter
decisions.reason: In the middle of a field "the house" is most likely a simple shelter where workers rested out of the sun.

decisions.choice: on her feet ... (Balanced); working ever since (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Stood" here means she has stayed at work; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal keeps "stood".

decisions.choice: She asked me
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the foreman is reporting Ruth's own request to him.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶל־ר֜וּת הֲל֧וֹא שָׁמַ֣עַתְּ בִּתִּ֗י אַל־תֵּלְכִי֙ לִלְקֹט֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה אַחֵ֔ר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א תַעֲבוּרִ֖י מִזֶּ֑ה וְכֹ֥ה תִדְבָּקִ֖ין עִם־נַעֲרֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Boaz to Ruth, [have] you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this, and thus stay close with my young women.
pieces: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go to glean in any other field, and do not move on from this one. Stay here close to my young women.

L.8: And Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, my daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and also do not pass on from this [one], but keep close here to my young women.

R.8: Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Do not go off to pick up grain in any other field. Do not leave this one. Stay here with the young women who work for me.

decisions.choice: have you not heard?: listen to me
decisions.reason: The question is a polite way of asking for attention: "listen carefully".

decisions.choice: my daughter: an older man speaking kindly
decisions.reason: Naomi calls Ruth "my daughter" (verse 2), and Boaz does the same. It is a warm address from an older person to a younger one, and suggests that Boaz is older than Ruth (3:10).

decisions.choice: keep close: stay with, cling to
decisions.reason: The verb dabaq is the one used of Ruth clinging to Naomi (1:14). Boaz asks her to keep close to his young women, and she does (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Listen to me (Balanced); Listen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have you not heard?" is given its sense; Literal keeps the question.

records.source: עֵינַ֜יִךְ בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־יִקְצֹרוּן֙ וְהָלַ֣כְתִּאַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן הֲל֥וֹא צִוִּ֛יתִי אֶת־הַנְּעָרִ֖ים לְבִלְתִּ֣י נָגְעֵ֑ךְ וְצָמִ֗ת וְהָלַכְתְּ֙ אֶל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְשָׁתִ֕ית מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשְׁאֲב֖וּן הַנְּעָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Your eyes [be] on the field which they harvest, and you will go after them. [Have] I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And [when] you are thirsty, you will go to the vessels and drink from what draw the young men.
pieces: Keep your eyes on the field they are harvesting, and follow along after the women. I have ordered the young men not to lay a hand on you. And when you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink from the water the young men have drawn."

L.9: [Let] your eyes [be] on the field that they are harvesting, and go after them. Have I not commanded the young men not to touch you? And when you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what the young men draw."

R.9: Watch which field they are working in, and follow the women there. I have told the young men not to bother you. When you are thirsty, go and drink from the water jars the young men have filled."

decisions.choice: after them: after the young women
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine: Ruth is to follow the young women of verse 8, who come behind the reapers binding the sheaves.

decisions.choice: touch: harm or harass
decisions.reason: To "touch" someone can mean to strike, harm or molest them (Genesis 26:11, 29). A foreign woman alone in the fields could be mistreated; Naomi sees the same danger in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the young men draw water for her
decisions.reason: Water was usually drawn by women (Genesis 24:11), and a foreign gleaner might expect to serve others. Here the men of Boaz's household draw it and she drinks freely.

decisions.choice: I have ordered (Balanced); I have told (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question "have I not commanded ...?" expects the answer yes, so Balanced and Readable state it plainly; Literal keeps the question.

decisions.choice: the women; the water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "them" is and what is drawn.

records.source: וַתִּפֹּל֙ עַל־פָּנֶ֔יהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו מַדּוּעַ֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ לְהַכִּירֵ֔נִי וְאָּנֹכִ֖ינָכְרִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And she fell on her face and bowed down to [the] ground and said to him, why have I found favor in your eyes, to take notice of me, and I [am] a foreigner?
pieces: Ruth fell face down and bowed to the ground. She said to him, "Why have I found such favor with you, that you would take notice of me, when I am a foreigner?"

L.10: And she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your eyes, that you take notice of me, when I [am] a foreigner?"

R.10: Ruth bowed down with her face to the ground. She said to him, "Why are you so kind to me? Why do you care about me? I am a foreigner."

decisions.choice: take notice of me ... a foreigner: a play on words
decisions.reason: "Take notice of" (hakkir) and "foreigner" (nokhriyyah) sound alike in Hebrew. A foreigner was someone others did not recognize or care about, yet Boaz has recognized her.

decisions.choice: foreigner: one from another people
decisions.reason: Nokhriyyah is a foreign woman, an outsider with no place in Israel by birth, a stronger word than the ger who has settled among the people. Ruth expects nothing as a Moabite (Deuteronomy 23:4).

decisions.choice: fell on her face and bowed: deep respect and thanks
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was the way to honor a superior and thank him (1 Samuel 25:23).

decisions.choice: two questions and a statement
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long question into short ones; the meaning is the same.

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַן בֹּ֨עַז֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ הֻגֵּ֨ד הֻגַּ֜ד לִ֗י כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂית֙ אֶת־חֲמוֹתֵ֔ךְ אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אִישֵׁ֑ךְ וַתַּֽעַזְבִ֞י אָּבִ֣יךְוְאִמֵּ֗ךְ וְאֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔ךְ וַתֵּ֣לְכִ֔י אֶל־עַ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָדַ֖עַתְּ תְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃
records.gloss: And answered Boaz and said to her, told, it has been told to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law after [the] death of your husband, and you left your father and your mother and [the] land of your birth and you came to a people that you did not know yesterday three days ago.
pieces: Boaz answered her, "I have heard the whole story of what you have done for your mother-in-law after your husband's death: how you left your father and mother and the land where you were born, and came to a people you had never known before.

L.11: And Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully told to me, all that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and [how] you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you did not know yesterday [or] the day before.

R.11: Boaz answered, "People have told me how good you have been to your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and the country where you were born. You came to live among people you did not know before.

decisions.choice: it has been fully told: the verb doubled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis: Boaz has heard the whole story, and in detail.

decisions.choice: left father, mother and the land of her birth
decisions.reason: The words recall God's call to Abraham to leave his land, his kindred and his father's house (Genesis 12:1). Ruth has made the same kind of break, with no promise given to her.

decisions.choice: yesterday, three days ago: before, in the past
decisions.reason: The pair of time words is a fixed way of saying "previously" (Genesis 31:2). She came to a people who had been strangers to her.

decisions.choice: never known before (Balanced); did not know before (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the time idiom; Literal keeps "yesterday [or] the day before".

records.source: יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה פָּעֳלֵ֑ךְ וּתְהִ֨י מַשְׂכֻּרְתֵּ֜ךְ שְׁלֵמָ֗ה מֵעִ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖את לַחֲס֥וֹת תַּֽחַת־כְּנָפָֽיו׃
records.gloss: May repay Yahweh your deed, and may be your wage complete from with Yahweh, God of Israel, whom you have come to take refuge under his wings.
pieces: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repay you for what you have done. May you receive your full wages from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, beneath whose wings you have come for refuge."

L.12: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} repay your deed, and may your wages be complete from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

R.12: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pay you back for what you have done. You have come to find safety under the wings of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you a full reward."

decisions.choice: under whose wings: in God's protecting care
decisions.reason: The picture is of a bird sheltering its young under its wings (Deuteronomy 32:11; Psalm 17:8; 36:8; 91:4). The word for wing, kanaf, also means the corner of a garment, and it comes back in 3:9, where Ruth asks Boaz to spread his "wing" over her. The man who prays for her shelter becomes the one through whom it comes.

decisions.choice: wages: the pay due to a worker
decisions.reason: Maskoret is a worker's wage (Genesis 29:15; 31:7), a fitting word in a harvest field. "Repay" and "complete" also come from one root (shalem): Boaz prays that God will pay her in full.

decisions.choice: take refuge: trust oneself to God for protection
decisions.reason: To take refuge in God is to rely on him for safety (Psalm 2:12; 5:12). By coming with Naomi and taking her God as her own (1:16), Ruth has put herself under the care of the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: order of the clauses
decisions.reason: Readable says first that Ruth has come to the LORD for safety, then gives the wish for her reward, in shorter sentences.

records.source: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר אֶמְצָא־חֵ֨ן בְּעֵינֶ֤יךָ אֲדֹנִי֙ כִּ֣י נִֽחַמְתָּ֔נִי וְכִ֥י דִבַּ֖רְתָּ עַל־לֵ֣ב שִׁפְחָתֶ֑ךָ וְאָנֹכִי֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽהְיֶ֔ה כְּאַחַ֖ת שִׁפְחֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And she said, let me find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and for you have spoken to [the] heart of your maidservant, and I, I am not like one of your maidservants.
pieces: She said, "May I go on finding favor in your eyes, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even one of your servant women."

L.13: And she said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your maidservant, though I am not like one of your maidservants."

R.13: Ruth said, "Sir, I hope you will always be this kind to me. You have comforted me. You have spoken kindly to me, and I am not even one of your servants."

decisions.choice: may I find favor: a wish, or thanks
alternatives: I have found favor in your eyes
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish ("may I find favor", that is, may your kindness continue) or as a grateful statement ("I am finding favor with you"). Either way she is thanking him.

decisions.choice: spoken to the heart: spoken kindly, reassured
decisions.reason: To speak to someone's heart is to speak words of comfort and encouragement (Genesis 50:21; Isaiah 40:2).

decisions.choice: maidservant: shifchah, a female servant of low rank
decisions.reason: Shifchah is a servant girl, one of the household's workers. Ruth calls herself his shifchah out of humility, yet says she does not even rank with his servant women. In 3:9 she calls herself his 'amah, a servant woman who could become a wife.

decisions.choice: servant, servant women (Balanced); servants (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "maidservant"; Balanced and Readable use the plain word.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: "My lord" is a polite address to a man of higher rank, not a title for God; Readable says "Sir".

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨ה בֹ֜עַז לְעֵ֣ת הָאֹ֗כֶל גֹּ֤שִֽׁי הֲלֹם֙ וְאָכַ֣לְתְּ מִן־הַלֶּ֔חֶם וְטָבַ֥לְתְּ פִּתֵּ֖ךְ בַּחֹ֑מֶץ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ מִצַּ֣ד הַקּֽוֹצְרִ֔ים וַיִּצְבָּט־לָ֣הּ קָלִ֔י וַתֹּ֥אכַל וַתִּשְׂבַּ֖ע וַתֹּתַֽר׃
records.gloss: And said to her Boaz at [the] time of the meal, come near here and eat from the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And she sat at [the] side of the harvesters, and he held out to her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had left over.
pieces: When mealtime came, Boaz said to her, "Come over here and help yourself to some bread. Dip your piece in the sour wine." So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he passed her some roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and still had some left over.

L.14: And Boaz said to her at the time of the meal, "Come near here and eat some of the bread, and dip your piece in the vinegar." So she sat beside the harvesters, and he held out roasted grain to her, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left over.

R.14: When it was time to eat, Boaz said to Ruth, "Come here and eat some bread. Dip it in the sour wine." So Ruth sat down with the harvesters, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. She ate until she was full, and there was still some left over.

decisions.choice: vinegar: a sour wine drink or dip
decisions.reason: Chomets is wine gone sour (Numbers 6:3). Workers dipped bread in it; it was a cheap, refreshing part of a field meal.

decisions.choice: roasted grain: heads of grain parched over a fire
decisions.reason: Fresh ears roasted over a fire were common food at harvest time and on a journey (Leviticus 23:14; 1 Samuel 17:17).

decisions.choice: ate and was satisfied and had left over: plenty after emptiness
decisions.reason: Naomi came home "empty" (1:21). Now Ruth eats her fill and has food to spare, which she takes home to Naomi (verse 18).

decisions.choice: sour wine
decisions.reason: "Vinegar" suggests a kitchen liquid to most readers; Balanced and Readable say what it was. Literal keeps "vinegar".

records.source: וַתָּ֖קָם לְלַקֵּ֑ט וַיְצַו֩ בֹּ֨עַז אֶת־נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ין הָֽעֳמָרִ֛ים תְּלַקֵּ֖ט וְלֹ֥א תַכְלִימֽוּהָ׃
records.gloss: And she rose to glean, and commanded Boaz his young men, saying, even between the sheaves let her glean, and do not humiliate her.
pieces: When she got up to glean, Boaz gave orders to his young men: "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not embarrass her.

L.15: And she rose to glean, and Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.

R.15: When Ruth got up to go back to work, Boaz gave orders to his young men. He said, "Let her pick up grain even where the bundles are lying. Do not make her feel ashamed.

decisions.choice: even among the sheaves: beyond the usual right
decisions.reason: Boaz grants what Ruth asked for (verse 7). Gleaners normally worked only where the reapers had already cleared the field; among the sheaves they could be suspected of taking the owner's grain.

decisions.choice: do not put her to shame: do not insult or humiliate her
decisions.reason: The verb means to shame or humiliate someone, by words or by treatment (1 Samuel 25:7, 15). No one is to treat her as a thief or an intruder.

decisions.choice: to go back to work
decisions.reason: Readable says that she went back to gleaning after the meal.

records.source: וְגַ֛ם שֹׁל־תָּשֹׁ֥לּוּ לָ֖הּ מִן־הַצְּבָתִ֑ים וַעֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם וְלִקְּטָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִגְעֲרוּ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And also pull, pull out for her from the bundles and leave [them], and she will glean, and do not rebuke her.
pieces: And even pull out some stalks from the bundles for her and leave them for her to glean. Do not scold her."

L.16: And also be sure to pull out [some] for her from the bundles and leave [them], and let her glean [them], and do not rebuke her."

R.16: Also pull out some stalks from the bundles on purpose and leave them for her to pick up. Do not speak harshly to her."

decisions.choice: pull, pull out: on purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: the reapers are to pull stalks out deliberately and drop them for her.

decisions.choice: bundles: handfuls of cut stalks
decisions.reason: Tsevatim, found only here, are the handfuls a reaper gathers before they are tied into sheaves.

decisions.choice: leave them: generosity beyond the law
decisions.reason: The law said a forgotten sheaf was to be left for the poor (Deuteronomy 24:19). Boaz tells his men to leave grain for Ruth on purpose, going beyond what the law required.

decisions.choice: on purpose
decisions.reason: Readable expresses the doubled verb with "on purpose"; Balanced uses "even", Literal "be sure to".

records.source: וַתְּלַקֵּ֥ט בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וַתַּחְבֹּט֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־לִקֵּ֔טָה וַיְהִ֖י כְּאֵיפָ֥ה שְׂעֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And she gleaned in the field until the evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah [of] barley.
pieces: So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to {{units:about 20 quarts|about an ephah}} of barley.

L.17: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.

R.17: Ruth kept picking up grain in the field until evening. Then she beat the stalks to knock the grain loose. She had {{units:about 20 quarts|about an ephah}} of barley.

decisions.choice: beat out: threshing by hand
decisions.reason: A small amount of grain was threshed by beating the stalks with a stick so that the kernels fell free (Judges 6:11). Ruth carries home grain, not bundles of stalks.

decisions.choice: about an ephah of barley: a very large day's gleaning
decisions.reason: An ephah was a dry measure of about 20 quarts. It is far more than a gleaner could expect from one day, enough to feed two women for many days, and it shows how much Boaz's orders (verses 15-16) helped her.

decisions.choice: about 20 quarts, with the ephah as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the ephah as the alternative; Literal keeps the ephah.

decisions.choice: beat the stalks to knock the grain loose
decisions.reason: Readable explains what beating out the grain means.

records.source: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ וַתָּב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וַתֵּ֥רֶא חֲמוֹתָ֖הּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־לִקֵּ֑טָה וַתּוֹצֵא֙ וַתִּתֶּן־לָ֔הּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹתִ֖רָה מִשָּׂבְעָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And she lifted [it] and came [into] the city, and saw her mother-in-law what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave to her what she had left over from her being satisfied.
pieces: She picked it up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gleaned. Ruth also brought out what she had left over after eating her fill, and gave it to her.

L.18: And she picked [it] up and went into the town, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave her what she had left over after she was satisfied.

R.18: Ruth carried it back into town, and her mother-in-law saw how much grain she had gathered. Then Ruth took out the food left over from her meal and gave it to Naomi.

decisions.choice: her mother-in-law saw
decisions.reason: The Hebrew as vowelled reads "her mother-in-law saw". The same letters could be read "she showed her mother-in-law", and some ancient translations have that. The scene is the same either way.

decisions.choice: what she had left over: the food from her meal
decisions.reason: This is the roasted grain left over at the midday meal (verse 14), which Ruth has kept for Naomi.

decisions.choice: how much she had gleaned
decisions.reason: "How much" makes clear what struck Naomi, the size of the gleaning (verse 17).

records.source: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ לָ֨הּ חֲמוֹתָ֜הּ אֵיפֹ֨ה לִקַּ֤טְתְּ הַיּוֹם֙ וְאָ֣נָה עָשִׂ֔ית יְהִ֥י מַכִּירֵ֖ךְ בָּר֑וּךְ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לַחֲמוֹתָ֗הּ אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשְׂתָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֧יתִי עִמּ֛וֹ הַיּ֖וֹם בֹּֽעַז׃
records.gloss: And said to her her mother-in-law, where did you glean today, and where did you work? May be the [one] taking notice of you blessed. And she told her mother-in-law [with] whom she had worked and said, [the] name of the man whom I worked with him today [is] Boaz.
pieces: Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" So Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man she had worked with. "The man I worked with today is named Boaz," she said.

L.19: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? May the one who took notice of you be blessed!" And she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today [is] Boaz."

R.19: Naomi asked her, "Where did you pick up all this grain today? Where did you work? Bless the man who was so kind to you!" Ruth told her mother-in-law whose field she had worked in. She said, "The man whose field I worked in today is named Boaz."

decisions.choice: may the one who took notice of you be blessed: Naomi sees a generous patron
decisions.reason: So much grain and food could only come from someone's special kindness. Naomi blesses him before she knows who he is. "Took notice of" is the word Ruth used in verse 10.

decisions.choice: Boaz: the name held to the end
decisions.reason: Ruth's answer puts the name last, so that it lands with weight, and Naomi reacts to it at once (verse 20).

decisions.choice: whose field she had worked in
decisions.reason: To work "with" a man here means to work on his land; Readable says so. Literal and Balanced keep "worked with".

decisions.choice: all this grain
decisions.reason: Readable adds what prompted the question, the amount she brought home.

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר נָעֳמִ֜י לְכַלָּתָ֗הּ בָּר֥וּךְ הוּא֙ לַיהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־עָזַ֣ב חַסְדּ֔וֹ אֶת־הַחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמֵּתִ֑ים וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ נָעֳמִ֗י קָר֥וֹב לָ֨נוּ֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ מִֽגֹּאֲלֵ֖נוּ הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said Naomi to her daughter-in-law, blessed [is] he by Yahweh, who has not forsaken his steadfast love with the living and with the dead. And said to her Naomi, near to us [is] the man; one of our redeemers [is] he.
pieces: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless him! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has not stopped showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love to the living and to the dead." Naomi went on, "That man is a close relative of ours. He is one of our family redeemers."

L.20: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed [is] he by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has not forsaken {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} steadfast love to the living and to the dead!" And Naomi said to her, "The man [is] near to us; he [is] one of our redeemers."

R.20: Naomi said to Ruth, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless him! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has kept on showing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love to those of us who are alive and to those who have died." Naomi also said, "That man is a close relative of ours. He is one of our family redeemers, who have a duty to help us."

decisions.choice: who has not forsaken: the LORD, rather than Boaz
alternatives: Boaz, who has not stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead
decisions.reason: "Who" could refer to the LORD or to Boaz. The same words are used of the LORD in Genesis 24:27, and Naomi had prayed that the LORD would show such love (1:8), so the LORD is the likelier subject: Naomi, who said the LORD had turned against her (1:20-21), now sees his care. If it refers to Boaz, Naomi is praising his kindness to the family.

decisions.choice: steadfast love to the living and to the dead
decisions.reason: Chesed is loyal, faithful love that keeps faith within a bond and goes beyond what duty requires. The living are Naomi and Ruth; the dead are Elimelech and his sons, whose family line and land are not forgotten (1:8; 4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: redeemer (go'el): the relative bound to help
decisions.reason: A go'el was a close relative with the duty to stand up for a family in trouble: to buy back land a relative had to sell (Leviticus 25:25), to buy back a relative sold into slavery (Leviticus 25:47-49), and to keep a dead man's name and line alive, as the related law of the brother-in-law requires (Deuteronomy 25:5-10). Naomi sees hope for her family's land and line in Boaz; chapters 3-4 show how.

decisions.choice: near to us: a close relative
decisions.reason: "Near" here means close by kinship. Naomi's words also hint that there may be others nearer (3:12).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6, Deuteronomy and Joshua 2:12, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: redeemer (Literal); family redeemer (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Redeemer" alone may suggest only a religious sense to modern readers; "family redeemer" shows that he acts for his relatives.

decisions.choice: who have a duty to help us
decisions.reason: Readable says briefly what a family redeemer was for.

records.source: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר ר֣וּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּ֑ה גַּ֣ם׀כִּי־אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֗י עִם־הַנְּעָרִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־לִי֙ תִּדְבָּקִ֔ין עַ֣ד אִם־כִּלּ֔וּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַקָּצִ֖יר אֲשֶׁר־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Ruth the Moabite, also that he said to me, with the young men who [belong] to me you will stay close until they have finished all the harvest which [belongs] to me.
pieces: Then Ruth the Moabite said, "He even told me, 'Stay close to my workers until they have finished all my harvest.'"

L.21: And Ruth the Moabite said, "He even said to me, 'Keep close to the young men who [are] mine until they have finished all the harvest that [is] mine.'"

R.21: Ruth, the woman from Moab, said, "He also told me, 'Stay with my workers until they have brought in all my harvest.'"

decisions.choice: the young men: the whole harvest crew
decisions.reason: Boaz had told her to keep close to his young women (verse 8); Ruth reports it with the masculine word, which can cover the whole group of workers. Naomi answers with the young women (verse 22).

decisions.choice: keep close: the same verb as in verse 8
decisions.reason: Dabaq, "cling, keep close", runs through the book (1:14; 2:8, 23).

decisions.choice: my workers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word that includes men and women; Literal keeps "young men", so the change from verse 8 can be seen.

records.source: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר נָעֳמִ֖י אֶל־ר֣וּת כַּלָּתָ֑הּ ט֣וֹב בִּתִּ֗י כִּ֤י תֵֽצְאִי֙ עִם־נַ֣עֲרוֹתָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִפְגְּעוּ־בָ֖ךְ בְּשָׂדֶ֥ה אַחֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Naomi to Ruth her daughter-in-law, good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, and they will not meet you in another field.
pieces: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is best, my daughter, that you go out with his young women. In someone else's field you might be harmed."

L.22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "[It is] good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that they do not fall upon you in another field."

R.22: Naomi said to Ruth, "My daughter, it is good for you to go out with the young women who work for Boaz. In another field someone might hurt you."

decisions.choice: fall upon you: attack or harm you
decisions.reason: The verb paga' means to meet, and often to meet with hostile intent, to attack (Judges 8:21; 15:12). Naomi fears what could happen to a young foreign woman alone among strangers.

decisions.choice: with his young women
decisions.reason: Naomi takes up Boaz's own instruction (verse 8) rather than Ruth's wording in verse 21: she is safest among the women.

decisions.choice: you might be harmed (Balanced); someone might hurt you (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they" means people in general; Balanced and Readable say it without naming who.

records.source: וַתִּדְבַּ֞ק בְּנַעֲר֥וֹת בֹּ֨עַז֙ לְלַקֵּ֔ט עַד־כְּל֥וֹת קְצִֽיר־הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים וּקְצִ֣יר הַֽחִטִּ֑ים וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב אֶת־חֲמוֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And she stayed close to [the] young women of Boaz to glean until [the] end of [the] harvest of the barley and [the] harvest of the wheat; and she dwelt with her mother-in-law.
pieces: So Ruth stayed close to Boaz's young women and gleaned until the barley and wheat harvests were over. And she went on living with her mother-in-law.

L.23: So she kept close to the young women of Boaz to glean until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.

R.23: So Ruth worked beside the young women in Boaz's fields, picking up grain until the barley and wheat harvests were over. All that time she lived with her mother-in-law.

decisions.choice: the barley harvest and the wheat harvest: about seven weeks
decisions.reason: Barley ripened first, around Passover, and wheat a few weeks later; the season ran about seven weeks, to the Feast of Weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9-10). Ruth came at its start (1:22).

decisions.choice: she lived with her mother-in-law: the season ends without a next step
decisions.reason: The chapter closes with Ruth still at Naomi's side, as she promised (1:16). Weeks have passed and nothing more has come of the meeting with Boaz, which sets the scene for Naomi's plan in 3:1.

decisions.choice: worked beside the young women in Boaz's fields
decisions.reason: Readable says what keeping close to the young women meant in practice.
